title: Priority-weighted surge mitigation and local KV eviction fix
creator: Daniel Park
body: Executive summary: Several customers on Dedicated pools experienced repeated request rejects and long coldstarts during a cross-region traffic surge. Root cause: an edge case in the burst allocation ledger coupled with local KV cache eviction behavior allowed tenant priority adjustments to temporarily starve warmup credits for small-tenancy slices. The autoscaler then downscaled cold pools due to a noisy warmup signal, amplifying the shortfall. This ticket coordinates a two-part fix (hotfix + resilience improvements), rollout, customer communications, and telemetry additions. Workstreams: 1) Patch burst ledger allocation to ensure atomic rebalancing of microburst credits across AZ partitions. 2) Adjust local KV eviction policy to retain prefix cache for tenants with recent burst activity (short TTL extension + LRU bias). 3) Add slow-path telemetry exposing per-tenant warmup credit balance and per-AZ microburst drift metric. 4) Deploy graceful fallback policy: when warmup credit depletion coincides with autoscaler downscale intent, prevent scale-down for 3 minutes and route low-priority traffic to compatible shared-capacity variant. Expected outcome: eliminate transient tenant starves during multi-AZ surges and reduce customer-visible coldstarts by >90% on affected flows.
comments: 2026-02-18 10:12 - Incident detect: Oncall alerted for repeated 429/503s from east-1 Dedicated pools; Pager duty routed to infra team. Initial blast radius included three enterprise tenants (two on dedicated reserved pools).

2026-02-18 11:05 - Triage: Warmup telemetry showed per-tenant credit depletion aligned with a regional marketing spike. Autoscaler telemetry indicated a downscale decision within a 60s window immediately after depletion. Hypothesis: allocator mis-slices burst ledger during multi-AZ rebalancing and local KV eviction evicted critical prefix-state causing requests to hit cold paths.

2026-02-18 13:22 - Mitigation (hotfix deployed): Rolled out rate-lift on affected tenants, temporarily increased reserved pool headroom for east-1, and disabled aggressive warmup decays. Immediate customer impact improved for 90% of requests. Patch id: runtime-hotfix/4821.

2026-02-19 09:40 - Root cause analysis: Reproduced race in burst ledger reconcile when AZ-affinity rebalancer migrated slot ownership. The code path that transfers microburst credits used a non-atomic two-step update; concurrent eviction of per-tenant KV prefix state caused warmup credit recalculation to undercount. Also discovered LRU policy favored global memory-heavy tenants and expelled small-tenant prefixes during surges.

2026-02-20 15:10 - Design discussion: Decided against increasing global default burst budget (too risky for multi-tenant fairness). Agreed on algorithmic fix: atomic compare-and-swap for ledger transfers + biasing KV eviction to favor recently-bursting tenant prefixes. Also agreed to add a transient scale-down holdback in the scale controller for entangled warmup-drain events.

2026-02-24 08:50 - PRs opened: runtime#4821 (atomic ledger transfer + scale-down holdback), cache-manager#193 (eviction biasing + short TTL extension), observability#77 (warmup-credit metric and per-az drift). Links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821

2026-02-25 18:00 - Integration testing: Ran chaos tests simulating AZ partition + sudden 5x QPS spike. New ledger transfers prevented credit loss in all runs (30/30). KV eviction bias reduced cold-path hits by median 95% in the suite. Observability shows new metric headroom_drift_east-1 trending flat after patch. Test run artifacts: https://console.redwood.ai/tests/chaos/482367

2026-02-26 11:30 - Customer comms: Drafted targeted emails for the three affected customers explaining root cause, mitigations, and next steps; CS reviewed and approved. Template: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcD-incident-communication-template

2026-02-27 07:40 - Canary rollout: runtime-1.22 canary in east-1 small cluster (10% traffic) for 24h. Early telemetry: warmup credit graphs look healthy; no regressions in latency or token cost. Canary link: https://console.redwood.ai/canaries/runtime-1.22/east-1

2026-02-28 20:15 - Rollout plan: Stage 1 (72h): east-1 full; Stage 2 (48h): remaining regions with staggered 12h windows; Stage 3: cutover scale-controller per-tenant holdback feature globally. Contingency: rollback if 10% increase in 5xx or token-cost delta > 8% observed.

2026-03-01 09:02 - Post-deploy monitoring: After east-1 full rollout, affected customers report stable behavior. Observability shows 92% reduction in coldstart 95p and no measurable headroom regressions. Closing actions: follow-up telemetry to keep headroom for 14 days, add unit tests for ledger transfer race, document change in runbook.
